title: India nears Chile trade deal, advances talk with Canada
summary:
India is nearing an FTA with Chile, while talks with Canada are progressing and SACU negotiations have begun, Piyush Goyal said. 
India also seeks expanded trade ties with Mercosur and other partners. 
Talks with GCC and Israel remain slow amid regional tensions, while US negotiations continue. 
India has developed manuals to strengthen institutional capacity for handling trade negotiations.

title: China's major industrial profits rise 15.5% in Jan-Sept 2026
summary:
China’s major industrial firms’ profits rose 15.5 per cent year on year in the first nine months of 2026, while September profits increased 14.4 per cent. 
High-tech manufacturing profits surged 52 per cent, accounting for 25.5 per cent of total industrial profits, as policy support and advanced manufacturing drove growth. 
Sustained growth hinges on domestic demand and broader industrial recovery.

title: India & Mexico to launch PTA talks to counter tariffs of up to 50%
summary:
India and Mexico will launch PTA negotiations this week to secure preferential market access for Indian exporters facing Mexican tariffs of up to 50 per cent on 1,463 product categories. 
Bilateral trade reached $7.83 billion in FY26. 
The proposed pact will focus on selected goods, while India advances trade talks with other partners, including Chile, Canada, the US and Mercosur.

title: South Indian cotton yarn sees mixed trend as cotton prices weaken
summary:
South India cotton yarn prices were mixed: Tiruppur combed yarn eased ₹3–5 (~$0.03–0.05) per kg as domestic and ICE cotton prices fell, while select Mumbai varieties rose ₹2–4 per kg on limited supply.
Gujarat cotton dropped ₹500–1,000 per candy as mills delayed purchases amid weak ICE futures and payment constraints.
All-India arrivals were 68,000–72,000 bales; Gujarat recorded 18,000–19,000.

title: Bangladesh's trade deficit widens 34% to $27.29 bn, a 3-year high
summary:
Bangladesh’s trade deficit widened 34 per cent to $27.29 billion in FY26 as imports rose 10.5 per cent and exports declined slightly. 
China and India accounted for the largest bilateral gaps. 
With garments making up 80.62 per cent of exports, the government is developing strategies for 18 key markets to diversify products, boost competitiveness and expand regional trade links.

The LYCRA Company will partner MarediModa 2026 in Cannes from October 27 to 29, marking 80 years since the bikini’s creation.
Its ‘Designed to move. Built to last.’ project with Carvico and Jersey Lomellina traces swimwear from the 1960s to today.
LYCRA XTRA LIFE fibre-enhanced fabrics are highlighted for comfort, fit and resistance to chlorine, sunscreen, heat and UV damage.

title: UAE-Benin trade deal targets $1 bn rise in Emirati exports by 2033
summary:
The UAE-Benin CEPA is expected to lift UAE exports to Benin by more than $1 billion by 2033, while Benin’s exports to the UAE could rise by $100 million.
The deal, signed in Abu Dhabi on October 25, covers about 97 per cent of current trade and will cut or remove many tariffs once ratified.
Non-oil trade reached $2.15 billion in 2025 and $1.29 billion in H1 2026.

title: ICE cotton tumbles as rising stocks and firm dollar pressure prices
summary:
ICE cotton fell sharply as faster US harvesting, a firm dollar and rising stocks pushed December 2026 below range; it settled at 79.06 cents, down 1.42 per cent.
US harvest reached 52 per cent by October 25, above five-year average; stocks rose to 27,865 bales and volume was the highest since October 9.
Markets await the Federal Reserve, fund rolls and possible Indian duty-free import extension.

title: China’s FDI inflows rise 2.5% in September as decline eases
summary:
China’s foreign direct investment inflows fell 4.3 per cent year on year to 548.81 billion yuan in January-September 2026, with September inflows rising 2.5. 
Investment in high-tech industries surged 33.8 per cent, accounting for 41.6 of total inflows. 
Investment from France, Switzerland and the US also increased, as China pledged improved market access for foreign firms.

title: US brand Marc Jacobs targets China growth through I.T Group deal
summary:
WHP Global and G-III Apparel Group have partnered with Hong Kong-based I.T Group to accelerate Marc Jacobs’ growth across Greater China, their first international licensing agreement since acquiring the brand in September 2026.
I.T Group has acquired the existing regional operating business and will expand boutiques, digital commerce, wholesale and shop-in-shop sites.

title: Cambodia overtakes India in 9 US apparel categories: $770 mn swing
summary:
Cambodia overtook India in nine US garment categories in January-August 2026 after a $770 million reversal in import values, TexPro shows.
Its import value rose 8.06 per cent to about $2.02 billion, while India fell 24.05 per cent to about $1.95 billion.
China’s August rebound masked a 26.85 per cent January-August fall, while higher US apparel tariffs failed to produce clear sourcing winners.

title: Türkiye loses €117 mn in EU denim. Who gets Europe’s jeans orders?
summary:
TexPro shows China almost level with Türkiye in Europe’s cotton-bottoms trade, with EU imports under HS 620342 and 620462 up 2.56 per cent to $9.88 billion in January–July 2026.
Türkiye fell 9.84 per cent to $1.158 billion; China rose 19.36 per cent to $1.150 billion, with a $7.76 million gap.
Egypt expanded 43.60 per cent and Vietnam advanced 36.98 per cent; women’s bottoms outpaced men’s.

title: Paraguay's apparel imports rise 24.1%, exports up 24.6% in 3Q
summary:
Paraguay's apparel imports rose 24.1 per cent to $166.963 million in January-September 2026 (3Q), while exports increased 24.6 per cent to $109.439 million.
Trousers and shorts led both flows; T-shirts, coats, socks and shirts were other key categories.
The apparel trade deficit widened to $57.524 million from $46.704 million as higher import values outweighed export gains.

title: Canada's Gildan completes $490 mn HanesBrands Australia sale
summary:
Canada's Gildan Activewear has completed the sale of HanesBrands Australia to BBFIT Investments for approximately Au$700 million ($490 million) in cash. 
The company plans to use the net proceeds to repay outstanding debt. 
The divestment supports Gildan's ongoing integration strategy, with a focus on operational priorities, capturing synergies and strengthening its portfolio of brands.

title: Bangladesh garment workers’ council demands $260 minimum monthly wage
summary:
IndustriALL Bangladesh Council has demanded a $260 monthly minimum wage for Bangladesh garment workers, citing higher living costs and market volatility.
IBC said essentials, transport and medical costs had strained workers, alongside a 100 to 142 per cent rise for government employees.
It plans grade-wise wage proposals once the full wage board is formed.

title: Could Suez reopen in 2027 and cut costs for EU apparel?
summary:
Europe’s apparel supply chain may see most container lines return to the Suez Canal by early second quarter 2027, but lower freight bills are not assured.
TexPro says the EU imported $23.08 billion of selected cotton-heavy apparel from Bangladesh, China, India and Vietnam in 2025.
Demand weakness and capacity management could keep delivered costs under pressure for garment buyers.

title: Myanmar's apparel export dependence shifts from Europe to Asia
summary:
Myanmar's apparel exports fell 21.1 per cent year on year to $3.757 billion in January–September 2026, with Europe's share down to 53.57 per cent.
Europe-bound shipments dropped 25.1 per cent to $2.013 billion, while Asia-Pacific's share rose to 36.18 per cent after a milder decline.
Japan led destinations at $852.863 million, ahead of Germany, Poland, South Korea and Italy.

title: Jordan's apparel exports rise 2.9% to $1.45 bn in Jan–July 2026
summary:
Jordan's apparel exports rose 2.9 per cent year on year to JOD 1.029 billion (~$1.45 billion) in January–July 2026, data showed.
Knitted apparel drove growth, up 4.1 per cent and representing 98.2 per cent of clothing exports, while woven exports fell 37.6 per cent.
July clothing exports grew 8.5 per cent, helping the sector outperform national exports; apparel imports rose 4.7 per cent.

title: Canada's Lululemon appoints Tara Poseley to board of directors
summary:
Lululemon athletica appointed former Chief Product Officer Tara Poseley to its board, effective October 19, 2026, expanding it to 13 directors, including 12 independents.
Poseley, most recently CEO of Paula’s Choice Skincare, joins under the company’s cooperation agreement with founder Dennis “Chip” Wilson and brings more than 30 years of retail, apparel and beauty experience.
